name: Cold open on the first claim
description: Drop everything before the first sentence that makes a claim, asks a question, states a number or promises a payoff, so speech starts on frame one; no logo, greeting or title-first open. Long-form: thesis spoken within ~10 s, brand sting only after a spoken tease.

evidence.note: Measured on 23 videos with speech in this run (caption timing) and consistent with two published frame-level studies.

prevalence.basis: measured in this run (25 videos, 23 with usable speech; caption timing): first word at <=0.4 s in 23/23 (<=0.25 s in 22/23), median 0.04 s, median 10 words in the first 3 s. Secondary: all 13 Shorts in the PandaStudio study reach speech/payoff within 2.5 s; first visual change ~1.9 s in 54 viral Shorts (Viibeo).

currentSupport: strike/remove ops exist; needs a hook finder in the planner
detect: Word timings of the reference: first word onset, words spoken in the first 3 s (10 is the measured median), hook sentence type; scene detection for time to first visual change.
render: No new rendering: strike/remove the lead-in words, then re-run tighten. Planner rule picks the first qualifying sentence.
acceptance: Output first word onset <=0.25 s; first sentence classifies as claim/question/number/promise; no greeting tokens ("hey guys", "welcome back", "in this video") before it unless pinned by the creator; >=8 words in the first 3 s for talking-head Shorts.
examples: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rWssyQD1uMw&t=0s (first word 0.00 s: the title is the first line)

name: Hard stop after the payoff
description: No outro, no "follow for more", no fade: Shorts end within a beat of the last payoff word or on a 1.5-2 s completed-state card; long-form speech runs to within ~6 s of the final frame.

evidence.note: Reported by one 22-video study.

prevalence.basis: Secondary: no outro in any of 22 measured top videos (PandaStudio law 7); MKBHD drops to 2-5 cuts in the last 30 s but keeps talking to 99% of runtime.

currentSupport: remove op exists; needs a rule
detect: Time from last word end to final frame; presence of outro phrases in the last 10 s of the transcript.
render: remove trailing beats; optional end card via the existing title card frame.
acceptance: Last word end to final frame <=0.5 s (or = endCardSec); no outro phrase in the final 10 s unless pinned.

name: Alternating punch-in crops on beat boundaries
description: Each new idea-beat toggles between a wide and a tight framing (about 1.15x to 1.5x), centred on the face, so jump cuts read as escalation and a single camera fakes multi-cam coverage.

evidence.note: Reported by Hormozi and DOAC teardowns and editing guides.

prevalence.basis: Secondary: alternating ~1.5x crops in 3/3 measured Hormozi Shorts; DOAC alternates crops every 5-6 s on monologues; sermon clips add punch-ins on key lines (Church Media Training); 100->115% punch zooms (EditorDuel). Not observable in this run.

currentSupport: per-beat static zoom exists (treatment.zoom 1-2); needs an alternation preset and face-centred crop
detect: Scene-cut times where the shot is the same camera but the face box scale changes by >10% (face detection on frames either side of a cut).
render: ffmpeg crop+scale per beat (already supported); add face-box anchoring and the alternation pattern in the planner.
acceptance: Consecutive beats alternate scale; face centre stays within the middle third; zoomed beats never crop the top of the head on 9:16; output sharpness at 1.5x acceptable from 4K or 1080p source (warn below).

name: Word-timed captions with one emphasis rule
description: Burned captions on every spoken word in Shorts: 1-4 words per screen (median 3), a new group every ~0.8-1.0 s, high contrast, centre-to-chest band; exactly one emphasis mechanism per video (weight OR colour OR box) on the operative word; optional active-word pop or karaoke fill; per-speaker colour.

evidence.note: Reported consistently by frame-level teardowns (PandaStudio Hormozi/DOAC/7 laws) and church-media guides; not observable here.

prevalence.basis: Secondary: burned captions in all 13 measured Shorts, 1-6 words per screen, one emphasis style (PandaStudio); Hormozi 1-4 words (median 3), groups every 0.8-1.0 s, white bold mixed case, emphasis by weight; DOAC 1-3 words, bold caps outline, host yellow/guest white; sermon clips: captions mandatory, single line <=22 chars (Church Media Training, ReachRight); MrBeast Shorts in Komika Axis (Shorty). Not observable in this run.

currentSupport: captions exist (wordsPerScreen, position incl. chest, preset, uppercase); needs per-word timing animation, emphasis choice and speaker colours
detect: OCR on sampled frames: words per caption screen, caption swap interval, vertical band, case, colour histogram of text pixels; emphasis = per-word style differences inside a screen.
render: libass via ffmpeg subtitles filter: ASS events per word group, \k or \kf for karaoke fill, \t(0,100,\fscx115\fscy115)\t(100,200,\fscx100\fscy100) for a pop, per-word {\b900} or {\c&H00EBFF&} for emphasis, \bord/\shad for contrast. No compositor needed.
acceptance: Every word appears within +/-50 ms of its onset; no screen exceeds wordsPerScreen or maxChars; captions never overlap a detected face box; exactly one emphasis style per render; text contrast ratio >=7:1 against sampled background.

name: Keep the texture (fillers, laughter, room feel)
description: Talking-head edits remove dead air between ideas, not personality: keep ums, laughs and room sound by default; keep long pauses on emotional material; strip fillers only for scripted or corporate pieces.

evidence.note: Weak measured signal (fillers/laughter surviving in ASR captions of 4 videos) plus reported studies.

prevalence.basis: measured in this run (25 videos, 23 with usable speech; caption timing): um/uh survive in the captions of 3 videos and laughter is tagged in 1 (ASR drops most fillers, so this is a floor). Secondary: fillers and laughter kept in all measured talking-head videos (PandaStudio); DOAC clips dry with laughter kept and grief clip pauses left long.

currentSupport: tighten.fillers flag exists; defaults should depend on format
detect: Compare reference ASR against a filler lexicon (um, uh, like, you know) and laughter tags; pause length around emotional keywords.
render: Planner defaults only (no renderer change).
acceptance: Default talking-head preset leaves fillers in place and only removes gaps; a "polished" preset removes them; laughter tagged by ASR survives every preset except "scripted".

name: Snappy pause and breath removal
description: Cut the space between phrases down to a small retained gap so speech runs at ~200+ words per minute with <=8% non-speech time; trims land between beats, never inside a sentence; breaths are cut or ducked.

evidence.note: Measured on 23 videos (caption-line timing; estimates, cannot see gaps under ~0.2 s); placement rule (between beats) is reported.

prevalence.basis: measured in this run (25 videos, 23 with usable speech; caption timing): 13 tight (est. pause share <=8% and <=2.5 pauses >0.5 s per min) + 6 moderately tightened of 23; median effective rate 210 wpm (IQR 183-220); median est. pause share 5%; in tight videos 90% of caption lines carry <=0.29 s of non-speech. Secondary: cuts placed on voice pauses (Viibeo); trims between beats (PandaStudio law 5).

currentSupport: tighten op exists (maxGapSec, padSec, fillers) with default pads 0.08 s in / 0.12 s out; needs gap targets per format, breath handling and click-free joins
detect: From reference word timings: pause share, pauses >0.5 s per minute, and the distribution of retained gaps at phrase boundaries (this run: tight <=8% / <=2.5 per min; p90 retained gap ~0.3 s). With audio: silencedetect (-35 dB, 0.08 s) on the voice; cut times from scene detection that coincide with speech gaps show jump cuts.
render: ffmpeg trim/atrim + concat with 10-20 ms acrossfade at every audio join; breaths found by VAD + energy/flatness classifier and either cut or gain-ducked with volume=enable windows; keep onsets (start at word.start - padIn).
acceptance: On a fixture recording: output est. pause share within +/-2 points of target; no joint gap above target+0.1 s unless a hold is marked; no clipped plosive/onset (spectral onset of the next word preserved); no clicks at joins (peak delta check); laughter kept when keepLaughter.

name: Zoning and safe areas
description: Reserve a caption band for the whole video, keep graphics in the top ~40%, never cover a face, never stack two text elements in one zone, and keep text out of the Shorts/Reels/TikTok UI areas.

evidence.note: Reported by one frame-level study (22 videos) and a second source on safe zones.

prevalence.basis: Secondary: held in all 22 measured top videos (PandaStudio law 6); keep text inside the Shorts safe zone (Viibeo).

currentSupport: caption positions exist (top, middle, chest, bottom); needs face-aware placement and platform UI masks
detect: Overlay boxes from OCR and graphics detection vs face boxes; overlap ratio and zone occupancy over time.
render: Layout solver before rendering: face detection per beat, then position captions/graphics in free zones; platform masks as constants.
acceptance: Zero frames where caption or graphic boxes intersect a face box; zero text inside the platform mask; never two text events in one zone at once.

name: Pattern-interrupt clock (no static stretch)
description: Something visible changes every 3-8 s in Shorts (median ~5 s; first change by ~2 s); in long-form the micro shot length is 3-6.5 s and the layout (talking head, B-roll, graphic) flips every 20-40 s. Flag and fill any static stretch.

evidence.note: Reported by three independent frame-level counts (Viibeo 54 Shorts, PandaStudio 22 videos, Tubefilter MrBeast); not observable here.

prevalence.basis: Secondary: 54 viral Shorts median shot 4.7 s, fastest quartile 2.8 s, 87% cut at least once (Viibeo); 3-8 s state changes in 13 Shorts and 7-13 changes/min long-form (PandaStudio); MKBHD 7.4 cuts/min; MrBeast 38 -> 23 cuts/min mid-video 2023 -> 2024 (Tubefilter). This run could not see cuts; 4 videos hold >2 s non-speech moments.

currentSupport: reference measurement of cuts/pace exists; needs a planner rule that fills gaps with zoom, keyword pop or cutaway
detect: Scene detection (ffmpeg select=gt(scene,0.3)) plus zoom/overlay change detection gives visible-change times; report median interval, first change time and the longest static stretch.
render: Planner inserts the cheapest filler (alternate punch-in, then keyword pop, then B-roll) wherever the projected change interval exceeds the threshold.
acceptance: On the rendered output, no static stretch >8 s in Shorts (or >60 s in long-form) unless the beat is marked as a deliberate hold; first visual change <=2.0 s.

name: Look presets (punchy grade, LUT, B&W, grain, vignette)
description: A consistent channel look: saturated high-contrast for entertainment, a LUT on sermon clips so they do not look flat in the feed, B&W for emotional beats, grain and vignette for documentary and essay tones.

evidence.note: Reported by published analyses or guides; no measurement in this run.

prevalence.basis: Secondary: apply your LUT before export (Church Media Training); bright, saturated grade (Shorty on MrBeast); LUT plus vignette in montages (DOR); dark backgrounds in 77% of DOAC frames (STEALSHOT). Estimate.

currentSupport: per-beat black and white exists; no grade/LUT/grain
detect: Colour statistics per shot: saturation and contrast distribution, B&W share (signalstats SATAVG), grain (high-frequency noise in flat areas), vignette (radial luminance falloff).
render: ffmpeg lut3d, eq, colorbalance, hue=s=0 (existing B&W), noise, vignette.
acceptance: Measured saturation/contrast of output within 5% of preset targets on a colour chart clip; B&W beats have SATAVG ~0.

name: Hook banner and end card
description: A banner naming the payoff at 0:00 (DOAC: white box, black caps) that exits by ~5.5 s; optionally a 1.5-2 s end card restating the title.

evidence.note: Reported by published analyses or guides; no measurement in this run.

prevalence.basis: Secondary: banner in 3/3 measured DOAC clips, gone by ~5.5 s (PandaStudio); intro bumper and end card in sermon repurposing guides (believers.site).

currentSupport: title card frame exists (full frame); needs an overlay banner that exits
detect: OCR text present from frame 0 that disappears within ~6 s and is not a caption of the speech.
render: ffmpeg drawbox + drawtext (or ASS) with enable between 0 and exitBySec; slide/fade with ASS \move/\fad.
acceptance: Banner visible from frame 0, gone by exitBySec; never overlaps captions or face; text <=2 lines.

name: Keyword pops instead of subtitles (long-form)
description: Long-form top channels burn no subtitles; instead 1-4-word pops land on the load-bearing words (timed so the move ends on the stressed syllable), plus 2-4 full-frame quote cards per video.

evidence.note: Reported: one measured long-form frame study (0/502 subtitle frames) plus motion-design references.

prevalence.basis: Secondary: 0 of 502 long-form frames from Ali Abdaal, MKBHD and Fireship had subtitle captions; keyword pops and quote cards instead (PandaStudio); word-by-word big type on stressed syllables at Vox, Johnny Harris, Cleo Abram (CraftingUI).

currentSupport: bigWord (one word per beat) exists; needs multi-word pops, styles and long-form defaults
detect: OCR text events that are not full transcripts: short phrases matching transcript keywords, with onset aligned to the spoken word.
render: ASS events (scale/fade in 8 frames) via libass; quote cards via the existing title-card frame.
acceptance: Each pop is complete on the stressed syllable +/-2 frames; <=4 words; never over a face; long-form preset turns full captions off by default.

name: Find the clip: one idea, payoff in the back half
description: From a long recording (sermon, podcast, stream, lesson) pick 30-90 s segments that hold one idea, open with a hook in the first 3 s and land the payoff at 55-85% of the clip; end right after the payoff.

evidence.note: Reported payoff placement (13 Shorts, 3 DOAC clips) and sermon-clip guides.

prevalence.basis: Secondary: payoff at 55-85% in all 13 measured Shorts and at 55/62/69% in 3 DOAC clips (PandaStudio); sermon clips 30-60 s, one idea per clip (ReachRight). Measured Short lengths in this run: 23-152 s.

currentSupport: planner can cut beats; needs transcript scoring for segments
detect: On a reference: locate the hook sentence and the payoff sentence (answer to the opening question/promise) in the transcript and report the payoff position as a share of runtime.
render: Planner output only (beats); no renderer change.
acceptance: Every proposed clip passes: length in range, a hook sentence in the first 3 s, payoff sentence between 55% and 85%, no second topic; a human rating panel prefers it over a random 60 s cut in >=70% of pairs.

name: Voice polish (denoise, EQ, compression, de-ess, breaths)
description: A clean, forward voice for phone speakers: high-pass, denoise, gentle compression, de-ess, breath reduction, then the existing loudness pass.

evidence.note: Reported by published analyses or guides; no measurement in this run.

prevalence.basis: Secondary: voice processed to sit forward with breaths reduced (EditorDuel on Hormozi); EQ and compression for vocal presence in sermon clips (believers.site). Estimate.

currentSupport: -14 LUFS loudness exists
detect: Noise floor in gaps, spectral tilt, crest factor and sibilance energy of the reference voice.
render: ffmpeg highpass, afftdn or arnndn, acompressor, deesser, then loudnorm (existing).
acceptance: Noise floor in gaps reduced by >=10 dB without speech-band artifacts; no pumping; -14 LUFS +/-1.

name: Music bed with ducking under the voice
description: A low music bed under speech that ducks when the voice is active and comes up in gaps; dry (no music) for podcast clips and emotional moments.

evidence.note: Music-only stretches measured from [Music] tags in 8 of 25 videos; bed levels and dry-vs-bed choices are reported.

prevalence.basis: measured in this run (25 videos, 23 with usable speech; caption timing): 8 of 25 videos have [Music]-tagged stretches without speech (beds under speech are not tagged). Secondary: sermon clips use a bed (Church Media Training; -18 to -24 LUFS suggested by believers.site); faint bed in 1 of 3 Hormozi Shorts; DOAC 3/3 dry (PandaStudio).

currentSupport: loudness to -14 LUFS exists; no music track
detect: Separate voice and accompaniment (source separation) and measure bed loudness under speech vs in gaps; [Music] tags in captions mark music-only stretches.
render: ffmpeg sidechaincompress (voice as sidechain) or volume automation from VAD, amix, then loudnorm to -14 LUFS.
acceptance: Voice-to-music level difference >=12 dB while speaking; bed returns within releaseMs in gaps; integrated output -14 +/-1 LUFS, true peak <= -1 dBTP.
examples: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DDRP89Lizrg&t=5s ([Music] beat right after the hook line)

name: Face-tracked vertical reframing
description: Turn 16:9 sermon, podcast or stream footage into 9:16 with a crop that follows the speaker smoothly, with manual fixes where tracking fails.

evidence.note: Reported as a standard step in sermon-clip workflows.

prevalence.basis: Secondary: Auto Reframe is a standard step in sermon-clip workflows (Church Media Training, believers.site); estimate for other clip niches.

currentSupport: aspect op exists (vertical/wide/square/original); subject tracking to be confirmed
detect: Reference is 9:16 with a subject that stays centred while the background shifts (crop path visible in background motion).
render: Face/person detection per frame (or every 3rd frame) -> smoothed crop path -> ffmpeg crop with sendcmd or per-segment crop; no compositor needed.
acceptance: Face centre stays inside the middle 40% of width >=95% of frames; crop velocity has no spikes above a set limit; no black bars.

name: Sound effects on accents
description: Whooshes on zooms and transitions, pops/clicks on text, risers before reveals, impacts on cuts; density is a style dial: an SFX on nearly every cut (MrBeast), sparse (modern Hormozi), none (DOAC, podcast clips).

evidence.note: Reported by published analyses or guides; no measurement in this run.

prevalence.basis: Secondary: impacts, whooshes and risers stitched to nearly every MrBeast cut (Shorty); sparse SFX in Hormozi style (EditorDuel, PandaStudio); DOAC clips have none; zooms ship with a swoosh by default in one creator-derived AI editor (PandaStudio agents guide). ASR cannot tag SFX, so this run could not count them.

currentSupport: not supported
detect: Onset detection on the non-speech residual (after voice separation) aligned to cut/zoom/text times; classify transient type (whoosh, pop, impact).
render: ffmpeg adelay + amix of SFX samples at event times, then the existing loudness pass; sample library with licences in AssetSchema.
acceptance: Each SFX onset within 20 ms of its visual event; never masks a word (voice-band energy check); density matches preset.

name: Pull the payoff forward (teaser and redacted hook)
description: Copy the strongest line to 0:00 as a teaser, optionally muting the operative words behind a card so the viewer waits for the payoff, then cut back into the story; or open on the most extreme moment and rewind.

evidence.note: Reported in 2 of 3 DOAC clips and MrBeast style guides; small samples.

prevalence.basis: Secondary: DOAC uses a redacted pull-forward in 1 of 3 measured clips and a banner frontload in another; MrBeast cold-opens on the most extreme moment (Shorty, infinitecreation); sermon guides open on the best line (ReachRight).

currentSupport: move op exists; needs a mute-words op and a cover card
detect: A sentence near the start that repeats (fuzzy match) later in the transcript; muted span inside the opening sentence (silence while the mouth moves).
render: insert beat (duplicate) at index 0 + a new mute-span op (volume=0 window) + title card overlay; ffmpeg only.
acceptance: Teaser beat duplicates a later beat; the muted span is exactly the chosen words (+/-40 ms); the full line plays unmuted later; total length change equals teaser length.

name: B-roll cutaways matched to the words
description: Insert short literal cutaways where the speaker names something concrete (1.5-4 s), from own footage, screen captures or licensed stock; the share varies by style from 0% (modern Hormozi, DOAC) to ~43% of frames (MKBHD).

evidence.note: Reported by frame-level studies of MKBHD, DOAC and Hormozi plus sermon guides; share varies 0-43% by style.

prevalence.basis: Secondary: MKBHD 43% B-roll frames; DOAC 0-6.5% of runtime, only on concrete nouns; Hormozi modern Shorts zero B-roll (PandaStudio); sermon clips use stock footage over parts that do not need the talking head (Church Media Training).

currentSupport: full-frame broll and split frames exist with assets; needs noun/phrase matching, sourcing and placement rules
detect: Layout classification of sampled frames (talking head vs B-roll vs graphic); share of runtime and insert length distribution; alignment of inserts with transcript nouns.
render: Existing broll/split frames in ffmpeg; work is in matching (transcript NER + search) and licensing.
acceptance: Each insert starts within 0.2 s of its trigger word; share within the preset range; every asset carries origin and licence (AssetSchema).

name: Ken Burns pans on stills and archival
description: Slow pan and zoom across photos, documents and archival images used as B-roll, so stills feel like footage.

evidence.note: Reported by published analyses or guides; no measurement in this run.

prevalence.basis: Secondary: photo pans 15 and collages 25 of 212 indexed explainer motion-graphics moments (Artiphik); slow push-ins on photos in the Vox style guide. Estimate overall.

currentSupport: card frame shows still images; no pan
detect: Still image (no internal motion) with uniform global zoom/translate over time.
render: ffmpeg zoompan (or crop with t expressions) on the image asset; upscale first to avoid jitter.
acceptance: No sub-pixel jitter (render from >=2x resolution); move covers the whole beat; framing never shows image edges.

name: Slow drift zoom over holds
description: A slow continuous push-in or pull-out (a few percent over the beat) on any hold longer than ~8 s so no frame is ever fully still; the video-equivalent of Ken Burns.

evidence.note: Reported in one Hormozi teardown; drift magnitudes from the Raylight measured library.

prevalence.basis: Secondary: slow push-in holds a 15 s listening shot in a Hormozi call-in clip (PandaStudio); measured product-film scale moves are mostly small (1-8%) eased drifts (Raylight library).

currentSupport: not supported (zoom is static per beat)
detect: Frame-to-frame scale change with no cut: optical flow or face-box size trend across a shot.
render: ffmpeg crop with time expressions (w=iw/(1+k*t), x,y centred on the face) then scale; or zoompan for stills. Sub-pixel smoothness needs scaling from a larger source frame.
acceptance: Scale changes monotonically by the set amount with no visible stepping at 30/60 fps (frame-difference of the face box smooth); no drift on beats shorter than minBeatSec.

name: Listicle counter pill and progress bar
description: A persistent numbered pill above the caption line that increments per list item (a completed item roughly every 4 s), and an optional thin progress bar.

evidence.note: Reported by published analyses or guides; no measurement in this run.

prevalence.basis: Secondary: numbered pill in Hormozi listicles (PandaStudio); progress bar drawn by an AI short-video renderer (Viibeo). Estimate overall.

currentSupport: not supported
detect: OCR finds a small persistent number that increments in sync with spoken ordinal words.
render: ffmpeg drawbox/drawtext with enable windows per item; progress bar via drawbox with width expression w=iw*t/T.
acceptance: Counter increments within 100 ms of the spoken ordinal; bar reaches 100% at the last frame.

name: Lower thirds, name tags and spec cards
description: Speaker name and title in podcasts and sermons, spec cards and credit tags in reviews, entering with a 200-300 ms slide/fade and leaving faster than they enter.

evidence.note: Reported by published analyses or guides; no measurement in this run.

prevalence.basis: Secondary: spec cards and credit tags in reviews (PandaStudio); measured product-film position moves median 218 ms, fades 100 ms (Raylight library). Estimate overall.

currentSupport: not supported
detect: OCR text box in the lower third that appears once per speaker for 2-5 s.
render: Static or ASS \move + \fad in wave 1; eased custom curves in the compositor later.
acceptance: Enters and exits within the set durations +/-1 frame; exits faster than it enters; never over a face or captions.
examples: Raylight motion reference library: shots 21233b523c33/1-3, f3c523c84569/1, f41065d6467c/2 (product films measured frame by frame)

name: Screen-recording and screenshot zoom-pans
description: Eased zoom into the part of a screen capture, screenshot or document being talked about (1-2 s moves in long-form, ~1 s in Shorts), optionally following the cursor, then back out.

evidence.note: Reported by published analyses or guides; no measurement in this run.

prevalence.basis: Secondary: zoom defaults of 1.0 s (Shorts) to 1.5-2.5 s (long-form) in an AI editor built from creator measurements (PandaStudio); screen recordings <1% of MKBHD frames but central in tutorial/dev content (Fireship study). Estimate overall.

currentSupport: not supported
detect: Scale change of a screen-like (UI) frame without a cut; text size increases smoothly.
render: ffmpeg crop+scale with eased time expressions (sendcmd keyframes) from a high-resolution capture; cursor position from capture metadata or detection.
acceptance: Target region fills >=60% of frame at full zoom; motion eased (no velocity jump at start/end); text legible at 1080x1920.

name: Camera follows the voice (multi-speaker clips)
description: For podcasts, interviews and call-in Q&A: switch to the active speaker exactly at turn boundaries, show the listener only as 1-1.5 s reaction cutaways under continuing speech, and colour-code captions per speaker.

evidence.note: Reported (DOAC frame-level teardown); this run only saw the call-in turn pattern in 2 Hormozi Shorts.

prevalence.basis: Secondary: DOAC 7 switches in 115.6 s, a cut every 4.1-6.3 s, speaker-coloured captions (PandaStudio); this run: 2 Hormozi call-in Shorts show long caller turns (est. pause share 16-22%).

currentSupport: not supported (needs diarization and per-speaker crop regions)
detect: Diarize the reference audio and compare speaker-turn times with cut times (switch within +/-100 ms of a turn = voice-following).
render: ffmpeg: per-speaker crop windows (from face tracks) selected per segment; reaction cutaways as video-only inserts over the speaker audio (needs split edits, see j-l-cuts).
acceptance: >=90% of speaker turns get a switch within 150 ms; no switch inside a word; reaction cutaways keep audio continuous (no gap in the voice track).

name: Cut to the music beat
description: Detect beats and onsets in a music track; land cuts, punch zooms and impacts on strong beats; let slow sections hold; used in montages, food and travel sequences, gaming and sports highlights.

evidence.note: Reported in gaming-montage guides; this run only saw 2 music-carried Shorts.

prevalence.basis: Secondary: beat-marker cutting, impact on the drop (DOR, Mark Studios gaming guides); content study of 100 TikToks favours fast pacing with music (DOAJ). This run: 2 Shorts are carried by music with almost no speech; 8 have [Music]-tagged stretches.

currentSupport: not supported
detect: Beat-track the reference audio (onset envelope + tempo) and measure the share of cuts within 40 ms of a beat; >50% indicates beat sync.
render: Beat tracking offline (e.g. aubio/librosa-style onset detection) then beats snap cut points; ffmpeg renders; audio mixed with amix/sidechain.
acceptance: >=80% of cuts within 40 ms of a detected beat; no cut inside a spoken word; music ends on a phrase boundary or fades in <=0.5 s.

name: Animated callouts (arrows, circles, underlines, boxes)
description: Strokes that draw on in ~160-200 ms to point at a detail in the frame, a screenshot or a document: circles, arrows, underlines, highlight boxes, then a quick fade.

evidence.note: Reported by published analyses or guides; no measurement in this run.

prevalence.basis: Secondary: callouts are 22 of 212 indexed explainer motion-graphics moments (Artiphik); Cleo Abram is on camera only 5-25% of her Shorts with an annotated, zooming world doing the work (PandaStudio); path reveals measured at 160-200 ms (Raylight library).

currentSupport: not supported
detect: Thin high-contrast strokes appearing over footage within a few frames, growing along a path (frame differencing near the target).
render: Compositor: vector path with trim-path (stroke dash offset) animation on a custom ease; anchored to a fixed point, or to a tracked point once motion tracking exists. Static versions possible with ffmpeg overlay of a pre-rendered PNG sequence.
acceptance: Stroke completes in drawMs +/-1 frame; ends on the target box (IoU >0.8 with the intended region); stays clear of captions.
examples: Raylight motion reference library: shots 21233b523c33/1-3, f3c523c84569/1, f41065d6467c/2 (product films measured frame by frame)

name: Split edits (J/L cuts) and reaction cutaways
description: Let sound lead or trail the picture across a cut: the next speaker heard before seen, a listener reaction under continuing speech, B-roll starting a few frames before the word it shows.

evidence.note: Reported by published analyses or guides; no measurement in this run.

prevalence.basis: Secondary: reaction J-cuts twice per 138 s DOAC clip (PandaStudio). Mostly estimate.

currentSupport: not supported (beats tie picture and sound together)
detect: Cut times in video that do not coincide with audio edit points (speech continues across the picture cut).
render: Edit model gains separate audio and video in/out per beat; ffmpeg renders video and audio timelines separately, then muxes.
acceptance: Audio waveform continuous across a J/L cut; picture cut lands at the set offset +/-1 frame.

name: Hard cuts by default; flash, whip, zoom and slide on accents
description: Keep hard cuts as the default; reserve transitions for section changes and music drops: a 1-frame white flash, whip-pan blur, zoom-through, slide, glitch/RGB split, light leak.

evidence.note: Reported by published analyses or guides; no measurement in this run.

prevalence.basis: Secondary: measured creators cut hard (Hormozi semantic hard cuts; MKBHD and Fireship counted by scene detection); white flash on the drop and plain cuts in fast sections (DOR); blurred transition frames between topics in DOAC long-form (STEALSHOT). Estimate.

currentSupport: hard cuts only
detect: Frames between two shots with uniform brightness spikes (flash), directional blur (whip), or blended content (dissolve/slide) instead of an instant change.
render: ffmpeg xfade (fade, slideleft, zoomin, wipes, pixelize, radial...) plus color source overlay for flashes; whip = slide + gblur/avgblur on the crossing frames; light leaks as screen-blended overlay assets.
acceptance: Transition length within +/-1 frame; whip blur direction matches the slide; no transition inside a spoken word.

name: Split screen, picture-in-picture and speaker cutout
description: Speaker cut out over B-roll or a screen (green-screen look without a green screen), corner PiP over screen recordings, top/bottom splits for reactions or gameplay.

evidence.note: Reported by published analyses or guides; no measurement in this run.

prevalence.basis: Secondary: split layouts 0% in MKBHD (PandaStudio); green-screen B-roll part of the 2021 Hormozi clone look (PandaStudio); reaction/gameplay splits are an estimate.

currentSupport: split frame (B-roll over speaker) exists; PiP and background removal do not
detect: Two independent motion fields in one frame; a person region with a sharp matte edge over unrelated background.
render: Split and PiP are ffmpeg overlay/stack; cutout needs a person-segmentation matte (model) and compositor alpha blending with edge feathering.
acceptance: Matte edge error below threshold on a hair test clip; PiP never covers captions or the focus region.

name: Kinetic typography (lines build on the voice)
description: A line builds word by word with the narration: each word finishes an ~8-frame move on its stressed syllable, the key word takes weight or the one accent colour, the full line holds 9 frames x words + 30 frames, then leaves in one 10-frame fade; highlight-sweep marker strokes over quoted text.

evidence.note: Reported by published analyses or guides; no measurement in this run.

prevalence.basis: Secondary: typography is 56 of 212 indexed motion-graphics moments from Vox, Johnny Harris, Cleo Abram and others (Artiphik); timing rules from CraftingUI; highlight sweep is the most copied Vox move (Easy-Peasy guide).

currentSupport: not supported (bigWord is a single static word)
detect: OCR word appearance times vs stressed-syllable times from forced alignment; text boxes that grow word by word.
render: WebGL compositor: per-word layers with transform keyframes on custom cubic-bezier curves, masks for highlight sweeps; libass can only approximate (no masks, limited easing).
acceptance: Word completion within +/-1 frame of the stressed syllable; line exit faster than its entrance; one emphasis per line; renders identically in preview and export (frame-diff < threshold).

name: Emoji, stickers and meme inserts
description: Pop-in emoji/sticker overlays on punchlines and short meme clips or sounds (gaming, comedy, and the older business-clone look).

evidence.note: Reported by published analyses or guides; no measurement in this run.

prevalence.basis: Secondary: meme sounds and pop-up graphics as gaming signatures (Adobe Video World); absent from modern Hormozi (PandaStudio). Estimate.

currentSupport: icon title cards exist; no overlays
detect: Small non-photographic overlay appearing with a scale pop, often paired with an SFX onset.
render: ffmpeg overlay with enable and a scale expression (or pre-rendered pop animation); compositor later for springy bounce.
acceptance: Overlay appears within 1 frame of its cue; never over face or captions; asset licence recorded.

name: Speed ramps and slow-motion impacts
description: Ramp down to 25-50% speed into an impact or reveal, often with a 110-130% zoom, then snap back to full speed on the beat (gaming, sports, cooking reveals).

evidence.note: Reported by published analyses or guides; no measurement in this run.

prevalence.basis: Secondary: gaming montage guides (DOR, Mark Studios). Estimate for other niches.

currentSupport: not supported
detect: Optical-flow magnitude drops sharply while audio continues at normal pitch; duplicated/interpolated frames.
render: ffmpeg setpts per segment with stepped ramps; minterpolate for smooth slow motion (slow, offline); 120 fps sources preferred.
acceptance: Ramp curve matches the set speeds within 5%; no judder visible at 30 fps (no duplicated frame runs >2 without interpolation); audio not pitch-shifted unless asked.

name: Animated maps and data charts
description: Zooming annotated maps (country fill, callout lines, orbiting camera) and charts that grow at the moment the number is spoken; timelines that scroll with the decades.

evidence.note: Reported by published analyses or guides; no measurement in this run.

prevalence.basis: Secondary: infographics 77, charts 36, maps 22 and timelines 9 of 212 indexed explainer motion-graphics moments (Artiphik); five-property map camera moves (Vox-style guide). Estimate overall.

currentSupport: not supported
detect: Chart/map-like graphics (large flat colour regions, axes, labels) whose elements grow over time.
render: Compositor: vector chart primitives with eased growth; map tiles or a vector world map with label-free style and camera keyframes.
acceptance: Chart value equals the spoken number; growth finishes within +/-2 frames of the number; map labels legible at phone size.

name: 2.5D parallax on stills
description: Split a still into foreground and background layers (segmentation plus inpainting) and move them at different speeds with a slow push; paper textures and drop shadows for the Vox look.

evidence.note: Reported by published analyses or guides; no measurement in this run.

prevalence.basis: Secondary: 2.5D parallax between layers in the Vox-style guide (Easy-Peasy). Estimate.

currentSupport: not supported
detect: Different motion vectors for foreground and background within a still-derived shot.
render: Compositor: segment subject (matting model), inpaint background, two textured quads with independent transforms and a virtual camera.
acceptance: No visible halo at the matte edge at 1080p; background inpaint has no repeated texture artifacts in the revealed area.

name: Matte reveals, shape wipes and 3D camera moves
description: Images revealed through animated shapes, wipes between layouts, z-space layer moves and orbiting virtual cameras (product-film and explainer polish).

evidence.note: Reported by published analyses or guides; no measurement in this run.

prevalence.basis: Secondary: matte reveals and group moves throughout the measured product films (Raylight library); 3D is 28 of 212 indexed explainer moments (Artiphik). Estimate for creator videos.

currentSupport: not supported
detect: A frame region that grows along a geometric boundary while showing new content.
render: Compositor layer mattes (alpha/luma) with keyframed shapes; perspective camera.
acceptance: Matte edges anti-aliased; move timings match keyframes +/-1 frame.
examples: Raylight motion reference library: shots 21233b523c33/1-3, f3c523c84569/1, f41065d6467c/2 (product films measured frame by frame)

name: Motion-tracked labels and stickers
description: Text, arrows or blur that stay stuck to a moving object or person.

evidence.note: Reported by published analyses or guides; no measurement in this run.

prevalence.basis: Estimate; not reported in the measured creator studies.

currentSupport: not supported
detect: Overlay whose position correlates with an object track over time.
render: Point/box tracker (offline) produces a keyframe path; compositor attaches layers to it.
acceptance: Overlay stays within 2% of frame width of the target through the shot; no jitter at rest.
